title: Run-length heart-rate asymmetry fails to improve primary cross-database heart-failure prediction beyond conventional HRV and one-step asymmetry
abstract: Adding a three-or-more-increment run-asymmetry contrast increased external Brier loss by 0.00637 (joint participant bootstrap95% [-0.00251, 0.01838]); favorable source cross-validation did not establish incremental cross-database predictive utility.
